procedures.label: Replacing a lamp unit
procedures.summary: A summary of Panasonic's procedure, for finding the parts. Work from the operating instructions.
before: Panasonic recommends asking a qualified technician to replace the lamp unit.
Replace it only after the lamp has cooled, at least one hour after switching off. The inside of the cover is hot enough to burn.
The lamp is glass and contains mercury. It can burst if dropped or struck. On a ceiling-mounted projector, do not work directly under the lamp unit or with your face near it.
Do not loosen the cover fixing screw with the projector standing on end: the cover can fall open under its own weight and a lamp unit can drop out.
Use only the specified lamp unit, and the same type in both positions.

steps.text: Check the lamp indicators LAMP1 and LAMP2. The lamp unit whose indicator is lit red is the one to replace.
Set the MAIN POWER switch to OFF and disconnect the power plug from the outlet. Wait at least one hour and check that the lamp unit has cooled.
With a Phillips screwdriver, turn the lamp unit cover fixing screw counterclockwise until it turns freely.
Open the lamp unit cover slowly. Opening it quickly can damage the cover.
Turn the two fixing screws of the lamp unit counterclockwise until they turn freely.
Hold the lamp unit by its handle and pull it straight out.
Push in the new lamp unit, minding its insertion position. If it does not seat, take it out and push it in slowly. Forcing it can break the connector.
Tighten the two lamp unit fixing screws firmly.
Close the lamp unit cover so that its connector is inserted into the fan power connector securely.
Tighten the lamp unit cover fixing screw firmly.

after: The steps show lamp unit 1. Lamp unit 2 comes out the same way; its screws and handle are the pair nearer the left side.
The projector resets the runtime of a new lamp unit automatically.
Replace the matching air filter when you replace a lamp unit. One air filter comes with each replacement lamp unit.
If the power does not turn on afterwards, check that the lamp unit cover is attached.

procedures.label: Removing, cleaning and attaching the air filters
procedures.summary: A summary of Panasonic's procedure, for finding the parts. Work from the operating instructions.
before: Turn off the power first, following the switching-off procedure in the operating instructions.
Do the work where the projector is stable and nothing is damaged if an air filter is dropped.

steps.text: Clean or replace the air filters when the FILTER indicator lights red and the filter message appears on the screen.
Turn the lamp unit cover fixing screw counterclockwise until it turns freely, and open the cover slowly.
Press the button on the projector and pull the air filter case out.
Lift the air filters off the air filter case.
Vacuum the dust off each air filter. Do not wash them with water. If dust remains after cleaning, replace the air filter.
Seat each air filter securely on the rib of the air filter case.
Push the air filter case in securely until it clicks.
Close the lamp unit cover so that its connector is inserted into the fan power connector securely, then tighten the fixing screw firmly.

after: Make sure the air filter case is attached before using the projector. Without it the projector draws in dust, the FILTER indicator flashes red and a message appears for about 30 seconds.

The hinge of the lamp unit cover: drawn at its left edge; its exact line is not established.
Exhaust fans behind the cover louvres: two are drawn because the illustration outlines two and the cover has a fan power connector. Their size and mounting are stand-ins.
Markings on the lamp units: the numbers 1 and 2 are generated tags, not product markings.
The SDI button position and the SDI IN terminal position: Panasonic marks both for the PT-DZ870 only. They are drawn blank; what a PT-DW830 carries there is not established.
Connector bodies, the mains inlet type and the switch: schematic stand-ins.
Ribbed bars low on both sides, shown in the illustrations: not drawn. The operating instructions do not name them.
Horizontal position of the lens: drawn on the centreline, as the illustration suggests. Not dimensioned for this model.
Bottom detail beyond the named ports: ribs, ducts and the centre boss are not drawn.
Which variant a given unit is: the entry is the model. A nameplate would say.
